item.research_question: Can annealing treatment at different temperatures induce fine precipitates in CoCrFeNiNb0.2Mo0.2 high entropy alloy to enhance its strength while maintaining ductility?
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc-melting of pure elements (>99.9 wt%) followed by annealing at 600, 700, and 800 °C for 24 hours
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile testing at a rate of 1 mm/min; XRD (Cu Kα, 40 kV, 40 mA); SEM and TEM characterization
key_findings: The best overall mechanical properties were achieved in the alloy annealed at 700 °C.
The yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation at 700 °C are 727 MPa, 1.05 GPa, and 8.38%, respectively.
A new Cr2Nb type nano-scale precipitate with a hexagonal close-packed structure was formed, with an average dimension of 95 nm at 700 °C.
The volume fraction of the HCP phase increased from 0% at 600 °C to 10.7% at 700 °C and 15.5% at 800 °C.
The ultimate tensile strength of the 700 °C annealed alloy increased by nearly 40% compared to the as-cast alloy.
The elongation decreased by only less than 2% compared to the as-cast alloy at 700 °C.
The interface between the HCP precipitate and the matrix is semi-coherent.
At 800 °C, the precipitate size increased to an average dimension of 310 nm, leading to embrittlement.
item.mechanism: The precipitation of a considerable amount of nano-scale HCP phase, which is semi-coherent with the matrix, provides an excellent strengthening effect. At higher temperatures, Ostwald ripening drives the coarsening of the lamellar-structured Laves phase and the HCP precipitates, which reduces plasticity and leads to embrittlement.
item.limitations: The text states that at 800 °C, the increase in precipitate size and coarsening of the Laves phase leads to a reduction in plasticity, causing the tensile specimen to fracture just past the yield point due to alloy embrittlement.
quotes: The best overall mechanical properties were achieved in the alloy annealed at 700 °C.
A new kind of Cr2Nb type nano-scale precipitate with a hexagonal close-packed structure was formed, which is semi-coherent with the matrix.
Ostwald ripening is the underlying mechanism driving the coarsening of the lamellar-structured Laves phase.
